title: A Newly Discovered Trail of Cosmic Debris Illustrates How the End of the Solar System Could Look
gist: ESO astronomers using the Very Large Telescope found a two-ring debris disk with a gap around white dwarf J1328-1450, about 1,600 light-years away, likely the remains of its planetary system. The rings hint that at least two bodies, one a few kilometers wide and one possibly Pluto- or moon-sized, survived, offering a preview of the sun's fate in about 5 billion years.

insights.claim: ESO's Very Large Telescope revealed that white dwarf J1328-1450, about 1,600 light-years from Earth, is surrounded by a debris disk with two distinct gas rings separated by a gap, likely remnants of its former planetary system.

insights.claim: In about 5 billion years the sun will exhaust its fuel, expand into a red giant possibly engulfing inner planets, then shed its outer layers into a white dwarf, with surviving rocky bodies potentially forming a debris disk like J1328-1450's.
